run: 2026-10-11, by the sgit-ai CLI agent following the skill's eight checks by hand
threat_model: an external attacker without write access (fork PRs, issues, comments)
verdict: No exploitable vulnerabilities identified. All workflows reviewed and cleared.

checks.evidence: no pull_request_target anywhere; the only triggers are push to dev / main, workflow_dispatch, and the internal workflow_call (ci-pipeline__dev.yml:3-6, ci-pipeline__main.yml:3-6, ci-pipeline.yml:3)

${{ inputs.test_target }} and ${{ inputs.extra_packages }} are expanded inside run: blocks of the composite action (action.yml:31, 37, 44, 56); both come from workflow_call inputs set as literals by the two callers in this repository, so only a writer can change them. ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }} is used in with:, not run: (ci-pipeline.yml:213)

DOCKERHUB_USERNAME / DOCKERHUB_TOKEN are used only in publish-to-dockerhub, which runs only when should_publish_dockerhub is true (main only) and after publish-to-pypi succeeded; PyPI publishing uses OIDC (permissions: id-token: write), no long-lived PyPI token
no AI-agent step in CI; the Makefile/shell loaded is the repository's own at the pushed commit

every third-party action is pinned to a full SHA: owasp-sbot/OSBot-GitHub-Actions@c2af482d… (three uses; the trailing comment says 'dev' but the ref is the SHA), docker/setup-buildx-action@8d2750c…, docker/login-action@c94ce9f…, docker/build-push-action@ca052bb…; actions/checkout, setup-python, upload-artifact are also SHA-pinned

no workflow-level permissions: block, so jobs run with the repository's default GITHUB_TOKEN permissions; increment-tag needs contents: write to push a tag, the test jobs need only contents: read. A top-level 'permissions: contents: read' with job-level elevation for increment-tag and publish-to-pypi would be least privilege. Not exploitable from outside: nothing untrusted runs in these jobs
ubuntu-latest hosted runners; the only artifact is the mutation report (upload only); no cache action

notes: No workflow runs on pull_request, so a PR from a fork never executes CI here; that is the reason the external-attacker surface is empty, and also why CI feedback on a branch arrives only after a push to dev
The pip install line interpolates extra_packages into bash (action.yml:31); the callers' own comment documents the quoting rule for 'mcp<2'. Writer-controlled only
